name: Blockchain Security
description: The security discipline unique to smart contracts and decentralized systems, where code is immutable after deployment and bugs can lead to irreversible loss of funds. Covers automated analysis tools (fuzz testing, static analysis), the taxonomy of known smart contract vulnerabilities, randomness manipulation attacks, and the professional security toolkit (Slither, Manticore, MythX, Echidna, OpenZeppelin). Also covers version control practices essential for collaborative smart contract development.

subskills.name: Fuzz Testing & Static Analysis
subskills.description: Automated techniques for finding smart contract vulnerabilities before deployment. Static analysis: examining bytecode or source code without executing it to find known patterns (Slither, Semgrep-for-Solidity). Fuzz testing / property-based testing: generating random inputs to find states that violate invariants (Echidna for property testing, Foundry forge fuzz/invariant tests). Coverage-guided fuzzing. Mutation testing (checking if tests catch intentionally broken code). The difference between finding bugs (fuzzing) and proving absence of bugs (formal verification).

subskills.name: Common Smart Contract Threat Vectors
subskills.description: The canonical taxonomy of smart contract vulnerabilities: Reentrancy (The DAO hack — malicious fallback calls back into victim before state update; mitigated by Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern and ReentrancyGuard), Integer Overflow/Underflow (pre-Solidity 0.8.x, mitigated by SafeMath / Solidity 0.8 built-in checks), Access Control failures (missing onlyOwner modifiers, tx.origin vs msg.sender), Front-running / MEV (transaction ordering manipulation), Flash Loan attacks (manipulating protocol state within atomic transaction), Improper Delegatecall (storage collision with proxies), Uninitialized Proxies, Oracle Manipulation (Mango Markets exploit — $100M), Signature Replay attacks, Denial of Service (griefing, block gas limit attacks).

subskills.name: Randomness Attacks
subskills.description: The challenge of generating unpredictable randomness in a deterministic, public blockchain environment. Blockhash-based randomness is manipulable by miners/validators (they can withhold blocks). block.timestamp is manipulable within ~15 seconds. RANDAO (Ethereum's post-Merge randomness beacon) is better but still gameable over a 1-epoch lookahead. Commit-reveal schemes (two-phase: commit hash of secret, then reveal). Chainlink VRF v2 as the production standard for verifiable, manipulation-resistant randomness in NFT mints, games, and lotteries.

subskills.name: Slither — Static Analysis
subskills.description: Trail of Bits' Slither is the leading open-source Solidity static analysis framework. Runs 90+ built-in detectors covering: reentrancy, unused return values, arbitrary send, unchecked transfers, suicidal/self-destruct, incorrect ERC-20 implementations, and more. Outputs findings by severity (High/Medium/Low/Informational). Integrates with CI/CD pipelines. Slither-read-storage for reading contract storage slots. Slither's printer module for inheritance graphs, call graphs, and variable dependency analysis.

subskills.name: Manticore — Symbolic Execution
subskills.description: Trail of Bits' Manticore is a symbolic execution tool for EVM bytecode and binary analysis. Symbolic execution explores all possible execution paths by treating inputs as symbolic variables, finding inputs that cause assertion violations or unexpected states. Useful for finding subtle bugs that fuzzing misses. More resource-intensive than static analysis. Manticore's API for writing custom analyses, and how symbolic execution complements fuzzing and manual review in a professional audit workflow.

subskills.name: MythX — Security Analysis Platform
subskills.description: ConsenSys' MythX is a cloud-based smart contract security analysis platform combining multiple analysis techniques (static analysis, symbolic execution, fuzzing) into an API-accessible service. Integrates with Hardhat (hardhat-plugin-mythx), Truffle, and Remix. Provides a security score and vulnerability report. MythX Pro for deeper analysis. Distinction between MythX (commercial platform) and Mythril (open-source underlying tool — individual symbolic execution engine). Used in CI/CD for automated pre-deployment security scans.

subskills.name: Echidna — Property-Based Fuzzer
subskills.description: Trail of Bits' Echidna is the leading Solidity property-based fuzzer. Developers write invariant properties (Solidity functions prefixed echidna_) that should always hold, and Echidna generates inputs to try to violate them. Covers: writing meaningful invariants, corpus management, coverage-guided fuzzing, Echidna's configuration (testLimit, seqLen, shrinkLimit), and running Echidna in Docker or CI. Distinction between assertion testing and property testing modes. How Echidna's findings complement Slither's static analysis.

subskills.name: OpenZeppelin Contracts & Defender
subskills.description: OpenZeppelin Contracts: the industry-standard audited library for ERC tokens, access control (Ownable, AccessControl, Roles), security utilities (ReentrancyGuard, Pausable, PullPayment), governance (Governor, Timelock), upgradeability (TransparentUpgradeableProxy, UUPS), and math utilities. Always prefer audited OpenZeppelin implementations over custom ones. OpenZeppelin Defender: cloud-based smart contract operations platform — Relayer (gas-managed transaction signing), Sentinel (alert on events/transactions), Autotask (serverless functions), Upgrade (secure proxy upgrades with multi-sig).

subskills.name: Version Control for Smart Contract Projects
subskills.description: Git-based workflows for smart contract development: Gitflow (feature branches, release branches) vs trunk-based development, conventional commits for changelog automation, GitHub Actions / GitLab CI for automated Solidity compilation, linting (solhint), testing, coverage, and security scanning (Slither in CI). .gitignore for blockchain projects (node_modules, artifacts/, cache/, out/, .env). Semantic versioning for contract ABIs and libraries. Monorepo patterns (Turborepo, nx) for protocol + frontend + subgraph codebases.
